title: 3 Penn State wrestling questions 80 days (or so) before the 2026-2027 season starts: On the schedule, the lineup, more - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Pickel ,
8 hours ago
Penn State Nittany Lions wrestling head coach Cael Sanderson (back) reacts in the 165-pound championship final of the Big Ten Wrestling Championships at Bryce Jordan Center. (Mandatory Credit: Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images) Penn State wrestling is now about 80 or so days away from kicking off its latest national title defense. College teams can hold their first dual meet as early as but no earlier than Oct. 30 . As the season approaches and the Lions are sort of in the news , we look at three key offseason questions still facing head coach Cael Sanderson’s team.

What will Levi Haines do? The NCAA continues to fight back against a recent Colorado court ruling that, as of this moment, gives athletes from the Class of 2022 who never took a redshirt year one final season of eligibility. That, of course, means two-time NCAA champ and four-time All-American Levi Haines could be back a part of the 2026-2027 Penn State wrestling lineup if he wants to be. The program seems to be for it. But, Haines has yet to comment on the possibility.
“Well, obviously, we’d love to have Levi back another year, so I’m going to lean into that. Like, yeah, let’s go,” Sanderson recently told FloWrestling .
There is no rush to make an announcement, considering the fact that Haines continues to train at the Nittany Lion Wrestling Club in State College. However, it won’t keep fans and others from endlessly wondering what his final decision will be.
Of course, the courts will have a say, too. If the NCAA eventually wins its appeal of the injunction that allows for this possibility, then Haines and other classmates who are already returning to football and basketball teams across the county would be out of luck. With that said, the organization’s track record in legal proceedings is abysmal, which makes it more likely than not that Class of 2022 athletes in the same situation as Haines will get a final year if they want to do it. And the final call will have an impact on the Lions’ lineup this winter.
More: Projecting the 2026-2027 Penn State wrestling lineup if Levi Haines returns to the Lions
Will Jayden James delay his enrollment? Speaking of eligibility issues, star Penn State Class of 2026 signee Jayden James also has a decision to make. While he is able to join the Lions and start his freshman season this year, he also could delay his enrollment becuase he is not yet 19 and thus start his five years to complete five seasons clock in 2027-2028. It is not currently clear if this possibility is the hope of some fans on the Internet or a legitimate possibility. A decision will need to be made before the fall semester starts.
More: What’s on deck for Penn State wrestling as the offseason continues? Ono’s debut, U20s, more
When will Penn State release its 2026-2027 non-conference schedule? Very few college wrestling teams already have their 2026-2027 schedule out. In fact, outside of Edinboro and Lock Haven, we have yet to find any others. So, the answer to this question — as is tradition — is probably no time soon. That will not stop other teams from releasing their schedules, though, and thus we will likely be able to piece together at least some of the Penn State non-conference dates this fall before the school actually announces them.
With all of that said, we do not expect the list to include Oklahoma State, even if David Taylor promises to save a date for Penn State annually moving forward .
